pages.text: Pond snails clung in the morning paddy. Curvy trails showed where they went. Mom picked them off, one by one.
"I want a basketful too." Dingding came with a basket.
"Lots in that patch earlier." Mom pointed below, then went to another job.
Dingding went there. Not one snail.
Sun shone hard. Water was lukewarm. "Where did they go?"
Search as Dingding might, none showed. The basket stayed empty.
Mom passed. "I saw them earlier. Look properly."
Dingding studied the mud floor. Curvy trails led toward grass shade.
Following them, Dingding found snails nestled together in the shade.
The basket quickly filled. One snail crept into the apron pocket. "Not cool in there!"
